issue_context.title: Sensors sensor.*_kib_s_received and sensor.*_kib_s_sent show unrealistic values
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The (re)introduced sensors `sensor.*_kib_s_received` and `sensor.*_kib_s_sent` in the UPNP integration show values that are way higher than my actual available bandwith (yes, I checked with speedtest.net if maybe my bandwidth changed, unfortunately it didn't ;-)).

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.10.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

everything prior to core-2021.10.0

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

UPNP

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/upnp/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
n/a
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
n/a
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Same issue with wrong values here.

If I kickoff a download running at around 80Mbit/s as reported by my download client and the OpenWrt router,  HA displays 11,486,293 KiB/s - if that helps.
I observed the values a bit while downloading, the reported values seem to be off by a factor of about >1000.
Thank you for this issue @haseat , @e10kstarfire. Unfortunately this is a bit hard for me to debug as my own router reports bogus values. Still, I'll try to investigate.
same here, values are about  *1000 higher than it should be

Same issue here, looks like the numbers are a factor of 1000 too large.
After a look at the code, it looks like the problem is in the raw sensor values on which the `kib_s`-sensors are based on(?).
Found the problem. Need to clean things up and I'll submit another PR... hopefully tomorrow.

I've believed that my internet provider make a Christmas days for me 🤔🤣
![Uploading Screenshot_2021-10-12-20-33-58-017_io.homeassistant.companion.android.jpg…]()

> same here, values are about *1000 higher than it should be

Actually 1024 times higher. It doesn't divide the value by 1024 to go from bytes to kilobytes.

review_comments: Why do both `async_setup_component` and set up the config entry? The former will already set up the config entry if we add it before calling `async_setup_component`? Normally we do one of these things not both.
